citationData.scope: Citations between papers in this map
citationData.note: References to the official LZ preprint are normalized to arXiv:2609.02823.

papers.title: Search for dark matter particle interactions in an extended nuclear recoil energy window with the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) experiment
papers.summary: LZ extends its nuclear-recoil search to roughly 270 keV and reports one event consistent with a 248 ± 23 (stat) ± 23 (sys) keV recoil. The maximum local significance is 3.4σ and the global significance is 2.6σ.
papers.takeaway: The experimental anchor: one unusual event, interesting enough to investigate but well below the threshold for a discovery.

papers.title: Inelastic Dark Matter Signature at High Recoil Energy in LUX-ZEPLIN and CRESST
papers.summary: Heavy halo dark matter scatters into a more massive state. A splitting near 350 keV suppresses lower-energy events, and the preferred region could be tested by a planned CRESST upgrade.
papers.takeaway: A generic endothermic explanation that shifts the recoil toward LZ's high-energy window.

papers.title: Higgsino Above the Sea of Fog
papers.summary: A thermal 1.1 TeV Higgsino with a several-hundred-keV neutral-state splitting can reach the event, though the rate depends strongly on the uncertain high-speed tail of the Galactic halo.
papers.takeaway: Places the event in a minimal thermal-Higgsino setting and emphasizes its astrophysical sensitivity.

papers.title: Higgsino Dark Matter Interpretation of the LUX-ZEPLIN 248 keV Nuclear-Recoil Event
papers.summary: A nearly pure, roughly 1 TeV Higgsino up-scatters through an off-diagonal Z coupling. The mass and interaction rate are largely fixed, leaving the neutral-state splitting to place the recoil.
papers.takeaway: A predictive Higgsino interpretation with less freedom than a generic inelastic model.

papers.title: TeV Higgsino Dark Matter from LZ Nuclear Recoil to Fermi-LAT Gamma Rays
papers.summary: A 1.1 TeV inelastic Higgsino is connected to a mild Fermi-LAT Galactic-center preference and to future gamma-ray tests with H.E.S.S. and CTAO.
papers.takeaway: Connects a Higgsino fit of LZ to independent indirect-detection channels.

papers.title: Fermionic Dark Matter Absorption and the High-Energy Event in LUX-ZEPLIN
papers.summary: Absorption of a roughly 247 MeV fermionic dark-matter particle on xenon converts its rest mass into a nearly monoenergetic recoil. The required benchmark is reported to be in strong tension with a KamLAND recast.
papers.takeaway: A distinct absorption mechanism that naturally lands at 248 keV but faces an important external constraint.

papers.title: A PQ-Symmetric High-Scale SUSY Interpretation of the LZ High-Energy Recoil
papers.summary: A 1.08 TeV Higgsino with a 0.3–0.35 MeV splitting is embedded in high-scale supersymmetry with a Peccei–Quinn sector and mixed Higgsino–axion dark matter.
papers.takeaway: Explains how the small Higgsino splitting might arise inside a broader high-scale theory.

papers.title: Dark Matter as the Z₂ Partner of the Standard Model Higgs Boson
papers.summary: An electroweak scalar doublet with a roughly 350 keV splitting produces the recoil through a fixed off-diagonal Z interaction and predicts pronounced annual modulation.
papers.takeaway: A non-Higgsino electroweak doublet with a sharp, testable seasonal prediction.

papers.title: Dark Matter at the Kinematic Edge: Interpreting the 248 keV LZ Nuclear-Recoil Candidate
papers.summary: A broad comparison finds ordinary elastic spin-independent scattering poorly suited to the isolated recoil, while spin-dependent and endothermic interactions remain viable. It develops pseudo-Dirac and thermal-Higgsino benchmarks.
papers.takeaway: A bridge between operator-level fits and concrete particle models with cosmological constraints.

papers.title: Strong Constraints on Higgsino Dark Matter from Solar Capture
papers.summary: The authors combine capture and annihilation in the Sun with IceCube's null result to argue for a splitting above 566 keV, which would exclude the thermal-Higgsino interpretation of the LZ event.
papers.takeaway: A direct challenge to the Higgsino island using solar capture and neutrino-telescope data.

papers.title: A Peccei-Quinn Origin for Inelastic Electroweak Dark Matter after LUX-ZEPLIN
papers.summary: Peccei–Quinn breaking splits a vectorlike electroweak doublet. The resulting subcomponent of dark matter can explain the recoil while axions provide the remaining abundance.
papers.takeaway: A mixed axion–electroweak scenario with a possible luminous signal.

papers.title: Inelastic Dark Photon Dark Matter for the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event and the Galactic Halo Gamma-Ray Excess
papers.summary: A 420 GeV dark photon up-scatters to a heavier vector partner through a scalar mediator. The same sector is arranged to retain a proposed explanation of a Galactic halo gamma-ray excess.
papers.takeaway: Links the LZ recoil to a second anomaly using inelastic dark-photon dark matter.

papers.title: Sub-TeV Singlino Dark Matter in light from Sagittarius A* and LUX-ZEPLIN Nuclear-Recoil Event
papers.summary: The paper discusses a sub-TeV NMSSM singlino in relation to LZ, but concentrates on gamma-ray detectability near black-hole dark-matter spikes rather than a detailed recoil fit.
papers.takeaway: Kept at the coastline because its connection to the LZ recoil is suggestive rather than a comparable quantitative fit.

papers.title: Inelastic Signatures of Electroweak Dark Matter
papers.summary: Coupled Majorana and Dirac electroweak multiplets generate a neutral-state splitting and off-diagonal Z interaction. Matching one event selects representation-dependent thermal benchmarks and correlated low-energy signals.
papers.takeaway: Generalizes the electroweak mechanism beyond a single representation and exposes correlated predictions.

papers.title: TeV Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ High-Recoil Event with Intermediate-Scale Electroweak Gauginos
papers.summary: A GUT-scale bino–wino cancellation yields the required Higgsino splitting with a wino near 120 TeV. The construction also discusses the newly raised solar-capture constraints.
papers.takeaway: A UV-level response to how a Higgsino could acquire the required small splitting.

papers.title: Confronting the Higgsino Interpretation of the LZ Event with the High-Energy Sideband
papers.summary: The authors argue that a full-density thermal Higgsino should also populate an empty higher-energy sideband. The strength of the tension depends on acceptance information that is not yet public.
papers.takeaway: A second major challenge to the thermal-Higgsino reading, focused on LZ's own sideband.

papers.title: Seasonal dark matter from the LUX-ZEPLIN high-energy event
papers.summary: Generic endothermic dark matter near the halo's kinematic edge can fit the event and should modulate annually by more than 50%, reaching nearly 100% in some regions.
papers.takeaway: Turns the fragile halo-tail dependence into a strong seasonal test.

papers.title: Atmospheric neutrino up-scattering explanation of LZ 2026 excess
papers.summary: Instead of halo dark matter, an atmospheric neutrino up-scatters on a nucleus to create a new massive state. The kinematic threshold removes lower-energy recoils while leaving an isolated high-energy event.
papers.takeaway: The incoming particle is an atmospheric neutrino rather than Galactic dark matter.

papers.title: Axion Portal Dark Matter and the LUX-ZEPLIN High-Recoil Event
papers.summary: A momentum-dependent pseudoscalar interaction produces elastic nuclear recoils without relying on an inelastic state change. A light pseudoscalar mediator embeds the operator in an axion-portal model.
papers.takeaway: Shows how elastic scattering can still favor high recoil when the interaction is momentum suppressed at low energy.

papers.title: Exothermic and Endothermic Inelastic Dark Matter Interpretations at LZ: Sideband Constraints and Future Prospects
papers.summary: The paper compares down-scattering, which can make a sharp recoil feature, with broader endothermic spectra and uses the empty high-energy sideband to separate and constrain them.
papers.takeaway: A bridge between the two inelastic coasts and the strongest current spectral discriminant.

papers.title: Exothermic Dark Matter at LZ
papers.summary: A heavier dark state down-scatters and releases a 0.5–1 MeV splitting, allowing 30–200 GeV dark matter to make a high-energy recoil. The model predicts still-higher-energy events in argon and germanium.
papers.takeaway: A concrete dark-photon realization of down-scattering with multi-target predictions.

papers.title: Inelastic from the Other Side: Xenon Excitation Signals in Light of the LZ High-Recoil Event
papers.summary: The authors calculate accompanying xenon nuclear-excitation signals for high-recoil models. Expected rates are generally at or below roughly ten percent of the elastic rate, so much larger exposures are needed.
papers.takeaway: Not a competing cause, but a possible future way to diagnose high-recoil dark-matter models.
